sources.note: Axia iQ product page (opened): iQ Main Frame 20.5 x 19 x 4.5 in (last value desktop to meter bridge); the page does not label the axes.

Axia iQ manual v1.3.1 (downloaded to a scratch folder outside the repo, text read): Appendix A dimension drawing "iQ Main Frame (8 faders + monitor controls)": 20.45 in (519.331 mm) x 19.01 in (482.881 mm) x 4.38 in (111.175 mm); each iQ frame has a connection panel with a Console (6-pin Molex), CANBus accessory, D-sub backup-PSU and IEC inlet; all audio I/O lives on the QOR.32 / StudioCore engine, so the catalog ports are a simplification placed on the console rear. Faders are 100 mm.
Axia StudioCore page (opened): 2RU engine, mic/line combos, RJ-45 line I/O, AES/EBU RJ-45, 4 GPI/O DB15, Livewire+ switch, IEC; gives the URL of the rear photo used for port placement.

StudioCore rear photo, straight-on (opened, 2000x650): scale 2.55 px/mm from the 2U height (227 px = 88.9 mm; an XLR combo is about 58 px = 23 mm, consistent); x from the left body edge, y from the bottom. Used only as the layout model for the simplified console rear: positions are copied onto the 519.3 mm wide console rear, centred.

iQ Main Frame (right) next to an expansion frame, straight-on view (opened, 2000x650): x scale 1.311 px/mm from the 519.3 mm frame width (681 px); depth scale 0.85 px/mm from the 100 mm fader slot (85 px), with the top-face y measured from the rear edge (photo y 203). The top-face x is mirrored (xMm = 519.3 - x_photo) because the face-local top view has the io (rear) edge at the bottom.
